sources.note: 'Mumeng (Zenag)' rows in the sound-correspondence tables; only a diachronic remark (printed p. 157-158) that unstressed vowels were deleted or became non-phonemic schwa in Proto Hote/Buang. No synchronic statement of Zenag stress placement.

sources.citation: Adams, Karen & Linda Lauck. 1985. Dialect survey of Mumeng dialect chain. In Papers in New Guinea Linguistics No. 22, 1-27. Pacific Linguistics A-63. Canberra: ANU. doi:10.15144/PL-A63.1
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No Zenag stress rule. Sec. 2.3 p. 11: 'Initial unstressed syllables in Patep always have the vowel schwa [ə].. for some words, Kumalu, Mumengtein, and Pelenkwa have a different stress pattern, so that not only does the initial syllable have a full vowel, but it also receives stress' -- Zenag is not named among the dialects that diverge from Patep. Chart F p. 12 has a Zenag column (word-final unstressed V+nasal = Vŋ, long vowels, vowel glides) but no stress row. Appendix B (pp. 16-27) gives a c. 110-item Zenag phonetic wordlist with stress marks (nə'lo 'nose', i'yai 'stomach', 'nɛnəbi 'skin',…
